text:
Jun: quick question on prefix cache — what if we expose a lightweight read-only 'shared view' API so other nodes can check residency without trying to acquire a lease? thinking about reducing duplicate prefills and churn
Ravi: what's the primary win vs complexity? cross-node prefills / avoid wasted work?
Jun: yes. bigger picture: node A wants to prefill hot prefix, but node B might already have it resident. A shared view could avoid duplicate fills. downside is stale info leading to races in eviction/prefill.
Marta: if we do that we need an epoch/version in the view. simple shape: {owner, epoch, flags} so readers can make conservative decisions.
Tess: we already have lease tokens for handoffs — could we extend token to be a short-lived 'read proof' that callers can use to justify not pre-filling? sketch: {prefix, epoch, owner_node, nonce, hmac} 
Ravi: HMAC is doable via sidecar key but keep in mind we have several states: pinned, soft-evict, intent-for-prefill. the shared view must surface state granularity, not just owner id.
Jun: agree. another race: A reads shared view -> sees non-resident -> starts prefill. B concurrently does eviction and frees slab -> churn. We need an 'intent' or CAS to avoid both prefill and evict racing dangerously.
Marta: proposal: cheap Bloom for presence checks (ok false positives), then confirm with view. For prefill we create an 'intent' claim with TTL so eviction checks see pending intent. Intent fields: {prefix, intent_epoch, claimant, ttl}. intent is ephemeral and ordered by epoch.
Tess: we should avoid relying on slow consensus (etcd) for per-prefix intents. Could use a fast gossip/mesh announcement or the existing lease assigner service as authoritative.
Ravi: what if we implement intent claims in the lease assigner (fast key-value with TTL) — eviction consults lease assigner + local intents. avoids adding a new persistent store.
Jun: good point. semantics we need: eviction path must be able to see active intents and, if present, demote rather than hard-evict. Also intents must expire on heartbeat loss, else partitioned intents block evicts forever.
Marta: TTL+heartbeat solves stale intents. default TTL maybe 5s with 1s heartbeat. Also we should add a fallback: if eviction finds only stale/unconfirmed intent (no heartbeat) it can proceed after a short backoff.
Ravi: metrics we need: duplicate-prefills, intent-conflicts, blocked-evicts, stale-intent-count. These will guide TTL tuning.
Jun: sketch of shared view response (cheap example):

```
{ "owner": "node-12", "epoch": "42", "flags": ["pinned"], "ts": "1610000000" }
```

Jun: and an intent claim example:

```
{ "prefix": "pfx:xyz", "intent_epoch": "43", "claimant": "node-7", "ttl": 5000 }
```

Tess: security note — if we allow proofs to be passed between nodes, sign/hmac them via sidecar so a malicious node can't fake claims. we can keep HMAC verification optional behind a feature flag for canary.
Marta: operationally, partitioning is tricky: if claimant loses connectivity but keeps thinking it holds intent, evictors should rely on heartbeat. documented grace windows required for compliance teams.
Ravi: also consider cost: extra RPCs on read path if callers validate view. we should aggressively cache view entries (very short TTL like 200ms) and prefer Bloom checks first.
Jun: implementation proposal: 1) Add shared view endpoint returning {owner, epoch, flags} with short TTL cache. 2) Intent claims implemented in lease-assigner with TTL+heartbeat. 3) Eviction consults lease-assigner+local intent table; on intent -> demote not evict. 4) Observability + metrics + canary rollout.
Marta: please enumerate flag enums (pinned, soft_pinned, prefill_intent, draining) and default TTLs in RFC. also define resolution rules when owner!=claimant and epochs mismatch.
Tess: I'll add the HMAC proto and sidecar integration notes. small RPC header: X-Shared-View-Proof: <base64(sig)> to carry proofs across calls.
Jun: ok I'll draft an RFC with those pieces. owners: Jun -> shared view endpoint + metrics, Ravi -> eviction consult + fallback, Marta -> intent protocol & flags, Tess -> HMAC/sidecar security design. @deploy-bot can we reserve a canary cluster?
deploy-bot: canary cluster reserved: cluster-canary-3
Ravi: sgtm, I'll sync with infra on lease-assigner capacity and keys.
Marta: I'll include experiment plan: start by exposing view read-only and count duplicate-prefills for a week, then enable intent protocol behind flag.
Tess: and I'll generate small compatibility shim so old nodes treat missing proofs as 'unknown' rather than failing.
Jun: perfect. I'll post RFC link when ready and schedule a 30m sync. thanks all! :rocket:
